survey <- na.omit(survey)

library('pacman')
pacman::p_load(foreign, ggplot2, dplyr, tidyr, tidyverse, gridExtra,
               car, haven, frequency, sjmisc, data.table, sjPlot,
               stargazer, margins, grid, questionr, rlang, haven, nnet, ggeffects, patchwork, knitr, kableExtra) 

cs3 <- c("#808080", "#FFCCCC", "#FF9999", "#FF6666", "#FF3333", "#CC0000", "#990000")

## Descriptives

ggplot(survey, aes(x = age)) +
  geom_bar(fill = "steelblue") +
  labs(title = "Age Distribution", x = "Age Group", y = "Count") +
  theme_minimal()

## PID Strength
ggplot(survey, aes(x = partisan_strength)) +
  geom_bar(fill = "darkred") +
  labs(title = "Partisanship Strength Distribution", x = "Partisanship Strength", y = "Count") +
  theme_minimal()

## Groups
ggplot(survey, aes(x = group, fill = age)) +
  geom_bar(position = "dodge") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = cs3) +
  labs(title = "Experimetnal Group by Age", x = "Group", y = "Count") +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1))

## self-monitoring and age
ggplot(survey, aes(x = self_monitoring, fill = age)) +
  geom_bar(position = "dodge") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = cs3) +
  labs(title = "Self-Monitoring by Age", x = "Self-Monitoring", y = "Count") +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1))

ggplot(survey, aes(x = self_monitoring)) +
  geom_bar(fill = "skyblue") +
  facet_wrap(~ age) +
  labs(title = "Self-Monitoring across Age Groups", x = "Self-Monitoring", y = "Count") +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1))

## self-monitoring and partisan_strength
ggplot(survey, aes(x = self_monitoring, fill = partisan_strength)) +
  geom_bar(position = "dodge") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = cs3) +
  labs(title = "Self-Monitoring by Partisan Strength", x = "Self-Monitoring", y = "Count") +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1))

ggplot(survey, aes(x = self_monitoring)) +
  geom_bar(fill = "steelblue") +
  facet_wrap(~ partisan_strength) +
  labs(title = "Self-Monitoring across Partisan Strength Groups", x = "Self-Monitoring", y = "Count") +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1))

ggplot(survey, aes(x = partisan_strength, fill = age)) +
  geom_bar(position = "dodge") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = cs3) +
  labs(title = "Partisanship Strength by Age Group", x = "Partisanship Strength", y = "Count") +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1))

# Self-Monitoring by Age Group How self-monitoring varies across ages
ggplot(survey, aes(x = age, y = self_monitoring)) +
  geom_boxplot(fill = "skyblue", color = "black") +
  labs(title = "Self-Monitoring Scores Across Age Groups",
       x = "Age Group", y = "Self-Monitoring Score") +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1))

# Self-Monitoring by Group (Control vs Experimental) Does self-monitoring differ between experimental groups?
ggplot(survey, aes(x = factor(group), y = self_monitoring)) +
  geom_boxplot(fill = "skyblue", color = "black") +
  labs(title = "Self-Monitoring Scores by Experimental Group",
       x = "Group (0 = Control, 1 = Experimental)", y = "Self-Monitoring Score") +
  theme_minimal()

# Partisan Strength by Group (Control vs Experimental) Does partisan strength differ between experimental groups?

ggplot(survey, aes(x = factor(group), y = partisan_strength_num)) +
  geom_boxplot(fill = "skyblue", color = "black") +
  labs(title = "Partisan Strength by Experimental Group",
       x = "Group (0 = Control, 1 = Experimental)", y = "Partisan Strength (Numeric)") +
  theme_minimal()

dd <- c("17-24", "25-34", "35-44", "45-54", "55-64", "65-74", "75-99")
p <- c("Independent", "Weak Partisan", "Leaning Independent", "Strong Partisan")


nomralmodel <- multinom(partisan_strength ~ age + race + gender + income + education + self_monitoring + group, data = survey)
## # weights:  104 (75 variable)
## initial  value 582.243632 
## iter  10 value 457.199436
## iter  20 value 439.862845
## iter  30 value 436.331921
## iter  40 value 435.552153
## iter  50 value 435.382761
## iter  60 value 435.367283
## final  value 435.367010 
## converged
self_agemn <- multinom(partisan_strength ~  race + gender + income + education + self_monitoring*age + group, data = survey)
## # weights:  128 (93 variable)
## initial  value 582.243632 
## iter  10 value 451.807030
## iter  20 value 432.319169
## iter  30 value 425.964770
## iter  40 value 424.175836
## iter  50 value 423.686646
## iter  60 value 423.496381
## iter  70 value 423.383237
## iter  80 value 423.364717
## iter  90 value 423.363355
## iter 100 value 423.359168
## final  value 423.359168 
## stopped after 100 iterations
self_groupmn <- multinom(partisan_strength ~ age + race + gender + income + education + self_monitoring * group, data = survey)
## # weights:  108 (78 variable)
## initial  value 582.243632 
## iter  10 value 456.777812
## iter  20 value 440.022153
## iter  30 value 436.149259
## iter  40 value 435.433252
## iter  50 value 435.267341
## iter  60 value 435.246475
## final  value 435.246361 
## converged
allmn <- multinom(partisan_strength ~ race + gender + income + education + self_monitoring * group * age, data = survey)
## # weights:  180 (132 variable)
## initial  value 582.243632 
## iter  10 value 449.175961
## iter  20 value 422.864622
## iter  30 value 408.111785
## iter  40 value 402.821651
## iter  50 value 399.694258
## iter  60 value 397.529341
## iter  70 value 397.014412
## iter  80 value 396.484894
## iter  90 value 396.327551
## iter 100 value 396.218729
## final  value 396.218729 
## stopped after 100 iterations
AIC(nomralmodel, self_agemn, self_groupmn, allmn)
##               df      AIC
## nomralmodel   75 1020.734
## self_agemn    93 1032.718
## self_groupmn  78 1026.493
## allmn        132 1056.437
nomralmodelLM <- lm(partisan_strength_num ~ age + race + gender + income + education + self_monitoring + group, data = survey)
self_ageLM <- lm(partisan_strength_num ~  race + gender + income + education + self_monitoring*age + group, data = survey)
self_groupLM <- lm(partisan_strength_num ~ age + race + gender + income + education + self_monitoring * group, data = survey)
allLM <- lm(partisan_strength_num ~ race + gender + income + education + self_monitoring * group * age, data = survey)

summary(nomralmodelLM)$adj.r.squared
## [1] 0.01272829
summary(self_ageLM)$adj.r.squared
## [1] 0.009297769
summary(self_groupLM)$adj.r.squared
## [1] 0.01038759
summary(allLM)$adj.r.squared
## [1] 0.01077621
mn1_pred <- ggpredict(nomralmodel, terms = c("age"))
mn1_pred$x <- factor(mn1_pred$x, levels = dd)
mn1_pred$response.level <- factor(mn1_pred$response.level, levels= p)
plot2 <- ggplot(mn1_pred, aes(x = x, y = predicted, colour = response.level)) +
  geom_jitter(shape = 19, width = 0.1, size = 3) +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(legend.position = "right") +
  scale_color_manual(values = c(
    "Strong Partisan" = "#0044CC",         
    "Weak Partisan" = "#6699FF",           
    "Leaning Partisan" = "#99CCFF",  
    "Independent" = "#808080"       
  ),
  breaks = c(
    'Strong Partisan',     
    'Weak Partisan',       
    'Leaning Partisan',
    'Independent')) +
  labs(x = "Age",
       y = "Predicted Probability",
       colour = "Response\nCategory",
       title = "Figure 1: Predicted Party Strength by Age")+
    theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1))

# Display the plot
plot2

kruskal_test_result <- kruskal.test(partisan_strength_num ~ group, data = survey)

kruskal_test_result
## 
##  Kruskal-Wallis rank sum test
## 
## data:  partisan_strength_num by group
## Kruskal-Wallis chi-squared = 0.007309, df = 1, p-value = 0.9319
pairwise_comparisons <- pairwise.wilcox.test(survey$partisan_strength_num, 
                                              survey$group, 
                                              p.adjust.method = "bonferroni")                                             
                                             
                                             
print(pairwise_comparisons)
## 
##  Pairwise comparisons using Wilcoxon rank sum test with continuity correction 
## 
## data:  survey$partisan_strength_num and survey$group 
## 
##   0   
## 1 0.93
## 
## P value adjustment method: bonferroni
# p = 0.428 > 0.05 There is no significant difference in partisan strength distribution between the control and experimental groups.
#Using non-parametric tests, you also find that there is no significant difference in partisan strength between control and experimental groups. The data does not support the idea that the softer question wording changed overall partisan strength scores.
## does selfmontioring differ across age groups
anova_age_self <- aov(self_monitoring ~ age, data = survey)
summary(anova_age_self)
##              Df Sum Sq Mean Sq F value Pr(>F)    
## age           6  3.419  0.5699   16.81 <2e-16 ***
## Residuals   413 14.000  0.0339                   
## ---
## Signif. codes:  0 '***' 0.001 '**' 0.01 '*' 0.05 '.' 0.1 ' ' 1
#anova is singicant p < 0.05 now we need to find out which age group differs, TukeyHSD
TukeyHSD(anova_age_self)
##   Tukey multiple comparisons of means
##     95% family-wise confidence level
## 
## Fit: aov(formula = self_monitoring ~ age, data = survey)

# 65-74 group has lower self-monitoring than 35-44 group

ktr
